tier_rationale: Kobo operates a real cloud (Kobo Store, Kobo Plus, OverDrive/Libby sync, Dropbox import), but the device's own firmware ships a documented Sideloaded Mode that completes setup and signs the device out with no Kobo account, and non-DRM ePub/PDF files transfer over USB with no login step described anywhere in Kobo's own instructions — so core reading function is fully achievable without ever touching Kobo's cloud.
the_unplug_test: Block Wi-Fi at the router and the Clara Colour keeps doing the one thing that matters: it opens and displays any EPUB, PDF or other supported file dragged onto it over USB, no Kobo account involved. Out of the box the setup wizard nudges you toward Wi-Fi and a Kobo Store account, but Kobo's own firmware includes a documented Sideloaded Mode that skips account creation entirely and disables only the cloud-dependent extras: the Kobo Store, Kobo Plus, OverDrive/Libby sync and Dropbox import. Firmware updates still appear to reach the device over Wi-Fi in this mode, so a permanently offline unit will fall behind on update checks it cannot make.

repairability.notes: iFixit lists the Clara Colour (N367) at 6/10 with battery, screen, front/back cover and motherboard replacement guides available.

sources.supports: Kobo's own support article: non-DRM ePub/PDF files copy directly to the KOBOeReader USB mass-storage drive from a computer; no account, login, or Kobo software is described as required for this transfer.

Manufacturer product page: 16GB storage, dual-band 802.11 ac/b/g/n Wi-Fi, Bluetooth for audiobooks, USB-C, 15 natively supported file formats including EPUB and PDF, $179.99 price, confirms this is the currently shipping model.

Describes Kobo's own Sideloaded Mode firmware feature, which lets a Kobo device operate fully signed out of any Kobo account while retaining Wi-Fi, purchased-book reading of already-downloaded titles, and Adobe DRM authorization; documents the SideloadedMode=true toggle Kobo itself ships in the device configuration file.

Community thread with posts through August 2025 confirming Sideloaded Mode still works on a current Clara BW unit (same firmware family as the Clara Colour) to skip Kobo account login entirely: connect at the 'let's get started' setup screen, add SideloadedMode=true to Kobo eReader.conf, restart. Notes Dropbox and Libby integration are disabled in this mode.

open_questions: Is there an in-UI 'skip account' option in the standard setup wizard, or does the account-free path always require the Wi-Fi-declined-plus-config-file procedure documented by the community? No first-party Kobo walkthrough of the account-free path end to end was found, only the underlying feature and its config toggle.
Does the device still check in with Kobo's servers for firmware updates while in Sideloaded Mode, and can that check be disabled?

Exact FCC ID for the Clara Colour (N367/N367B) was not located; Rakuten Kobo's other eReader and tablet models file under grantee ZJL, which is a reasonable prior but was not confirmed for this specific model.
notes: This is the direct contrast to Kindle: Kobo ships an account-free mode as a supported firmware feature rather than as an exploit, and its own help pages document USB sideloading of personal files with no account step. The catch is that the feature is not surfaced in the ordinary setup wizard as a menu option — a reader wanting it has to know it exists. Rakuten/Kobo has no entry in data/vendors.json and a light search turned up no documented incident of removed function or lost purchases; vendor_risk is scored 0 on that basis but the check was not exhaustive.
local_replacement_note: Kobo's own USB sideload path already replaces the store for personal libraries; pairing it with Calibre on a computer (library management, format conversion, metadata) reproduces the sync/organize function of the Kobo cloud entirely on hardware the owner controls.
